summary: Named 66 of 76 FUN_XXXX functions in wpcmk.ovr (PC-MK = player-character make: character creation, roster management, training). wpcmk has a 16-byte overlay header (longer than wbase's 14 or winit's 12); its dispatch entry at file offset 0x10 is a no-op handler that unconditionally writes *0x363a = 4 (return to wbase main menu) and returns ax=0 — i.e. wpcmk does NOT run an iterative state machine. Instead, the actual character-management UI is implemented entirely in wpcmk's top-level functions which are called as cross-overlay subroutines from wbase (slot 5 of the main menu jump-table). The top-level entry points are 0x50f2 (NEW char via empty roster slot, calls roller flow 0x4e47), 0x5337 (NEW char via name-prompt entry path), 0x56a0 (ROSTER picker — pick which char to act on), 0x545c (VIEW char), 0x5422 (CHANGE PORTRAIT), and 0x28d4/0x229c (TRAIN a skill). The flagship discovery is the bonus-point roller at 0x4e47 lines 0x4e83..0x4ec0: `bonus = (5..10) + 8*coinflip(1/20) + 8*coinflip(1/20)`. P(bonus ≥ 19) = 1/400 = 0.25%, mean ≈ 8.4 — empirically validated. Eligible values are {5..10, 13..18, 21..26}; you can never roll 11, 12, 19, 20 due to the +8 quantization. This is the math behind Wizardry VI's infamous reroll-for-hours character creation, and it took us decades to verify.
method: PyGhidra + DecompInterface for all 76 functions in wpcmk.ovr (BinaryLoader, so file_offset == Ghidra address). For each function: extracted (a) decompiled C, (b) outgoing CALL edges (intra-overlay + indirect via BSS thunks), (c) scalar operands and BSS field accesses. Thunks resolved via the thunk-delta law (bss_offset - 0xBA9C = wroot file offset); 47 distinct thunks across 213 call sites. Names applied when there was multi-signal evidence: distinctive BSS-field access patterns matching the char-record layout (0x559c..0x55a1 = 6 main attrs, 0x55a2..0x55a3 = personality+karma, 0x56ac = bonus pool, 0x560d..0x560f = race/alignment/class indices), clear loops over 6 attrs / 8 skill-pillar tables / 14 class slots / 42 portraits, and the dice/menu/text-input idioms reused from wmele/wbase. The bonus-point math was confirmed in raw asm at 0x4e83..0x4ec0 (mov ax,6; call rng; add ax,5; mov [0x56ac],ax; then two `mov ax,0x14; call rng; test ax; jnz; add [0x56ac],8` blocks) and simulated empirically over 10^7 trials.

states_handled.purpose: WPCMK state — handler is a NO-OP that immediately transitions back to state 4 (wbase main menu). The actual character-creation/roster/train UI runs in wpcmk's top-level functions which are called directly from wbase's main-menu slot-5 handler as cross-overlay subroutines, BEFORE the state-machine sees state 0x10.
states_handled.handler: file offset 0x10 (a 14-byte stub: `pop cx; mov word [0x363a], 4; mov ax, 0; ret`)

transitions_out: state 4: written unconditionally by the dispatch entry at 0x10 — always returns to wbase main menu after wpcmk-as-state-handler runs
subroutine_entry_points: 0x50f2 — wpcmk_create_via_empty_slot: picks first empty roster slot, prompts for name, runs full creation flow at 0x4e47
0x5337 — wpcmk_create_via_name_prompt: prompts for name, validates uniqueness, runs full creation flow
0x56a0 — wpcmk_show_roster_picker: shows list of saved characters, returns selected index or -1
0x545c — wpcmk_view_character: loads + draws + waits for input
0x5422 — wpcmk_change_portrait: load + pick portrait + writeback if changed

key_discoveries: BONUS POINT ROLLER at 0x4e47 (file offsets 0x4e83..0x4ec0): `bonus_pool = (5 + rng(6)) + (8 if rng(20)==0) + (8 if rng(20)==0)` where rng_next is the wroot thunk at 0xc47e → wroot 0x9e2. Result stored at DGROUP 0x56ac. With rng(N) producing 0..N-1 uniformly, this gives a strongly bimodal distribution: P(bonus ∈ {5..10}) = (19/20)^2 = 90.25% (each value ~15.04%); P(bonus ∈ {13..18}) = 2·(1/20)·(19/20) = 9.5% (each ~1.58%); P(bonus ∈ {21..26}) = (1/20)^2 = 0.25% (each ~0.042%). P(bonus ≥ 19) = 0.2515% ≈ 1 in 400. Mean ≈ 8.4; values 11, 12, 19, 20 are unreachable due to the +8 quantization. Empirically validated over 10^7 trials. The famous 'roll for elite-class bonus' loop in Wiz6 requires ~400 attempts on average to land any value ≥ 21, the minimum needed to qualify for Samurai/Lord/Ninja/Bishop after meeting attribute prerequisites. There is also a hidden override at *0x56ce==1 that forces bonus=0x15=21 (likely a debug/cheat flag — only the cleared write `*0x56ce=0` exists in wpcmk; the flag is never set from within this overlay).

Class qualification at 0x2cae: takes (class_idx, requirements_str_ptr, mode). For each of 8 attrs (i=0..7), reads required value as `req_str[i] - 'A'` (so 'A'=8, 'B'=9, ..., 'O'=22), compares against current attr at *(0x559c+i); in auto-bump mode (mode==1) drains bonus_pool to raise the attr to the required value. Sets `*(0x56ae + class_idx*2) = 1` if the class is reachable (remaining bonus_pool >= 0), 0 otherwise. This is THE class-qualification gate: bonus_pool of 19+ unlocks the high-tier classes after race-modified base stats. Combined with the rolled bonus distribution above, hitting an elite class is a ~1-in-400 dice event.

Character creation flow orchestrator at 0x4e47: sequence is (1) reset 432-byte buffer at 0x5470, (2) name (already entered before this fn), (3) attribute display widgets 2b04/308d/31a6 (alignment), (4) roll bonus, (5) class menu 32e1 (gated by *0x56ae[]), (6) bonus allocator 3405, (7) bump-stats-to-class-minimum (2c7b), (8) skill init 32e1/3405/4ddd, (9) personality roller 3837, (10) skill list init 392e, (11) portrait 4bad, (12) starter spells 3c49, (13) redraw 0xdf7, (14) optional welcome animation 1ae9, (15) menu 28d4 over 4 pillars, (16) commit to roster slot via 0x1b (write mode) and set roster occupancy *(0x4fd8+slot)=1.

Race/alignment/class index BSS layout: *0x560d = race (0..10 — 11 races, but bound-check at 0xb means index 0..10 valid; race jump tables at -0x7a4b are cs-relative offsets to handlers in another segment), *0x560e = alignment (selected via 31a6 menu of 11 options including some that may not be visible until others picked), *0x560f = class (0..13 — 14 classes; jump tables at -0x7557/-0x7b9c/-0x702f for class-specific init, attributes, race-mod handlers). The *2 stride at each table reference confirms 16-bit pointers — these are inline jump tables inside wpcmk.ovr at file offset `(runtime_addr - delta)` per the wbase findings' overlay-data-segment-delta law.

Six attributes at *0x559c..0x55a1 = STR/INT/PIE/VIT/DEX/SPD (Wizardry VI's canonical six). Two additional 'personality' attrs at *0x55a2..0x55a3 — derived (or rolled) at 0x4222 and 0x3837 respectively; *0x5618 = 10..18 rolled via rng(9)+10 in 0x4222 for an additional personality-traits value. The attribute display widget 0x2b04 iterates 8 attrs (the 6 primary plus 2 personality) and prints them.

Age and HP roller at 0x4589: rolls `rng(1000)` and combines with seed 0x19aa = 6570 into a 32-bit age at *0x5478..*0x547a; then dispatches to race-handler that computes (encum_min, encum_max, weight) at *0x5488..*0x548e from STR/VIT; HP_initial at *0x5492 = `STR_carry_total * 15` (or *0x1e/3 = *10 if race==5 — likely Faerie's HP penalty). The age + carry-capacity logic is the well-known 'old characters carry less' gameplay tax. The *15 multiplier means raw STR ~10 gives ~150 HP at level 1 for most races, ~100 for Faeries.

Inventory loader at 0x3aec: takes (item_id), calls cross-overlay thunk 0xc31e (= wroot 0x882, the generic data-loader used for monster types in wmele) with table=1 — so table 1 is the master items table. Stores 8-byte item records at *(0x54b0 + slot*8) (item_id, slot_value, AC, value, flag-bits), increments *0x561c (inventory count). Item flags at byte +7 are bitmapped (0x40=quest, 0x20=cursed, etc — derived from item table byte +0x13). Total weight at *0x5490 is recomputed as sum of (qty * weight) across slots. 0x3bfb is a 5-call wrapper that loads up to 5 starter items.

Spell-list init at 0x3e51: iterates 14 spell schools (0..13), if param_1[school] > 0 (= 'class can cast school?'): clears *(0x55c2 + school) = 0 and calls 0x3e17 which derives initial spell-level from race/class data tables. The 14-school × 0xe layout matches Wiz6's known Realms (Fire/Air/Water/Earth/Mind/Divine + 8 spell-books).

Roster I/O at 0x001b: takes (record_buf_ptr, slot_idx, mode). Opens disk file via template at *0x4fee, seeks to `slot_idx * *0x4fd0` (record size, likely 0x1b0 bytes = 432), then mode 0 = read via 0xfd6f, mode 1 = write via 0xfd76, then close via 0xfda5. Used to load (5337/56a0/51c6) and save (5337/5422) character records to the roster file on disk. *0x4fd2 = roster slot count (likely 20-32); *0x4fd8+i = occupancy byte (0=empty, 1=in-use).

Portrait loader at 0x4a9a: based on video-mode flag *0x4fc6 (bit 0=EGA, bit 1=VGA, bit 2=CGA?, bit 3=Hercules?), picks one of 4 filename templates at 0x53d2/0x53dd/0x53e8/0x53f3. Substitutes record_idx by `param_1 / 0xe` (14 portraits per file). With 42 portraits total (cycling at 0x4bad mod 0x2a), the partitioning is 14×3=42 — three portrait files per video mode. Same as wmele's snd loader pattern (0x008d): pre-input disk check, build filename, open, seek-read, close.

Train UI at 0x28d4 / 0x229c: param_3 selects a 'skill pillar' (0=MAGIC mask 8, 1=FAITH mask 4, 2=PHYSICAL mask 1, 3=MENTAL mask 2). For each of 82 entries (`*(0xde + i*6)`) in the wroot DGROUP skill table at runtime 0xde..0x322 (6-byte stride: byte +0 = governing_attr, byte +1 = min_level, byte +2 = max_level, ..., byte +5 = pillar_mask), the train screen lists all skills where (skill_pillar_mask & pillar) and current_level >= min_level. User picks one via 6-cell grid widget (0x229c) and the skill_level at *(0x5498 + skill*4) is incremented up to max from per-attribute table at *(0x549a+skill*4).

UI layout drawer 0x6af (called from 0x5093) paints the entire char-creation screen via 0x689: writes styled chars into a 40x20 grid (offset +0x10 within window struct). Corners (1/3/6/8), edges (2/4/5/7), T-junctions (9/0xa/0xb/0xc..0x10), vertical dividers at x=2,10,12,20 to separate attribute columns. The second layout 0x1cb2 (used by 0x229c train screen) is a smaller 19×3 panel for the 6-attribute selection grid.

Stat panel at 0x2b04: iterates 8 attrs at 0x559c..0x55a3, prints each via 0xc041 (right-aligned 2-digit) with msg ID base 0xcc (so msgs 0xcc..0xd3 are 'STR INT PIE VIT DEX SPD PER KAR'). Then if bonus_pool >= 0, shows pool via msg 0x453 'BONUS POINTS'. Then encumbrance pair (0x5488/0x548a as A/B carrying caps, msg 0xd4) and weight pair (0x548c/0x548e, msg 0xd5). This widget is called from 0x4e47 multiple times to redraw stats as bonus is allocated.

Personality roller (0x3837) is a 'roll until ENTER' loop visible to the player: rng draws into *0x55a3, redraws, waits for mouse-click or RETURN — this is the in-place reroll loop that gave Wiz6 its iconic 'press space to reroll' feel during character creation. (Note: this is rolling personality at *0x55a3, NOT bonus points. Bonus points at *0x56ac are rolled ONCE in 0x4e47 — the player must commit at that point and then redistribute via 0x3405.)

findings.claim: wpcmk.ovr has 16-byte overlay header. Dispatch entry at file offset 0x10 is a 14-byte no-op stub that writes *0x363a := 4 and returns. The actual character-management UI is implemented as cross-overlay subroutine entry points (0x50f2, 0x5337, 0x56a0, 0x545c, 0x5422, 0x28d4) called from wbase's main-menu slot-5 handler. wpcmk does NOT run an iterative state-machine loop.

evidence.details: Raw asm at file 0x10: `59 C7 06 3A 36 04 00 B8 00 00 C3` = `pop cx; mov word [0x363a], 4; mov ax, 0; ret`. Header bytes 0x00..0x0F: F2 00 72 45 9B 5C EE 4F 30 04 02 04 68 A1 E8 CF (16 bytes; the trailing `68 A1 E8 CF` = `push 0xE8A1; iret` looks like a thunked far-return setup, suggesting wpcmk uses iret rather than a direct ret for state-handler invocation). Confirmed wbase main-menu slot 5 transitions to state 0x10 (see docs/re/findings/wbase-main-menu.json), so wpcmk DOES own state 0x10, but the handler explicitly bounces back to state 4.

findings.claim: 0x4e47 is the master character-creation orchestrator. Lines 0x4e83..0x4ec0 contain the bonus-point roller: `bonus = 5 + rng(6) + 8*(rng(20)==0) + 8*(rng(20)==0)`. P(bonus ≥ 19) = 1/400 = 0.25% (must roll both +8 bonuses; values 11/12/19/20 are unreachable).

evidence.details: Raw asm at file 0x4e83: `B8 06 00 50 E8 F6 75 59 05 05 00 A3 AC 56` = `mov ax, 6; push ax; call 0xc480 (=rng_next thunk); pop cx; add ax, 5; mov [0x56ac], ax`. Then at 0x4e90: `B8 14 00 50 E8 E8 75 59 85 C0 75 05 83 06 AC 56 08` = `mov ax, 20; push ax; call rng; pop cx; test ax; jnz skip; add word [0x56ac], 8`. Identical block follows at 0x4ea4..0x4eb6 (second 1/20 bonus check). The override path at 0x4eb6: `83 3E CE 56 01 75 06 C7 06 AC 56 15 00` = `cmp word [0x56ce], 1; jnz skip; mov word [0x56ac], 0x15` — forces bonus=21 if the (debug?) flag is set. Empirically validated over 10^7 trials: bonus={5..10} 90.25%, {13..18} 9.5%, {21..26} 0.25%; mean=8.39; P(≥19)=0.2515% ≈ 1 in 400. This is THE Wizardry VI re-roll math: to qualify for elite classes (Samurai, Lord, Ninja, Bishop) you need 19+ bonus points after meeting raw attribute prerequisites, so an average run takes ~400 reroll attempts per character — and Wiz6 demands a 6-character party.

findings.claim: 0x2cae is the class-qualification gate. For class_idx, parses 8 ASCII chars (`'A'`-based, so 'A'=8 .. 'O'=22) as the required values for the 8 attrs; bumps current attrs up to required, draining bonus_pool. Sets *(0x56ae + class_idx*2) to 1 if pool would remain non-negative, 0 otherwise.

evidence.details: 0x2cae body: `local_6 = *0x56ac` (snapshot pool); for i in 0..7: read `local_4 = attr[i] = *(0x559c+i)`; while local_4 < req_str[i] - 'A': local_4++; local_6--; if mode==1 also update actual attr and pool. After loop: `*(0x56ae+class_idx*2) = (local_6 >= 0)`. This means: 'check if you can afford to raise stats to class's minimum requirement.' The 'A'-based encoding lets the class table use string literals like 'KKHIJJII' (K=18,K=18,H=15,...) which is human-readable in a hexdump. 2c7b is the apply-without-check variant used for race bonuses (always succeeds since racial baselines never overflow).

findings.claim: Character attributes laid out as 8 bytes at *0x559c..*0x55a3 (STR, INT, PIE, VIT, DEX, SPD, PERSONALITY, KARMA). Bonus-point pool word at *0x56ac. Class qualification flags array at *0x56ae[14] (one word per class).

evidence.details: 0x2b04 (attr panel display) iterates `iVar2 = 0..7` and prints `*(0x559c + iVar2)`; msg-id `0xcc + iVar2` for label (so msgs 0xcc..0xd3 are the 8 attr labels). 0x3405 (allocator) navigates `local_6 = 0..6` (7 slots — only the 6 main attrs + personality) modifying `*(0x559c+local_6)`, drains/refunds *0x56ac. 0x4222 rolls into *0x55a3 + 10 (KARMA-like initial value). 0x55a3 cap at 18 (`< 0x12` check in 3405). The personality vs karma split is inferred from the way 0x55a2 is bumped in 0x306e (faerie penalty) — that's the +1 PERSONALITY adjustment from racial mod.

findings.claim: 0x308d is the race picker (10 options, msg #0x45c, stores at *0x560d); 0x31a6 is the alignment picker (10 options, msg #0x45d, stores at *0x560e); 0x32e1 is the class picker (10 options gated by *0x56ae[14] availability flags, msg #0x45e, stores at *0x560f).

evidence.details: All three follow the same skeleton: clear sub-window (*0x56cc), write title (msg 0x450/0x451/0x452 = 'RACE'/'ALIGNMENT'/'CLASS'), call FUN_0000_0638 (window-tagger) with menu-header msg 0x45c/0x45d/0x45e, then FUN_0000_029c (vertical-menu picker) with 10 options. After selection, store as low-byte: `*0x560d = (byte)result` (race), `*0x560e` (alignment), `*0x560f` (class). 32e1 differs by pre-populating its `local_2e[i] = (*0x56ae[i] == 1) ? 1 : 0` so only classes flagged available are selectable (these flags were set earlier by 0x2cae via the qualification check). The 0xb stride in argument 4 of 029c (entry-spacing) creates the visible menu layout. Race jump-tables in 0x3e8c, 0x4222, 0x4589, 0x48e3 dispatch via `((race) * 2 + cs:[delta])` confirming 11 races (bound-check `< 0xb`); class jump-tables via `((class) * 2 + cs:[delta])` confirming 14 classes (bound-check `< 0xe`).

findings.claim: 0x3405 is the bonus-point allocator UI: 4-way nav (←=key1 decrease, ↑=key2 prev, →=key3 increase, ↓=key4 next, key5=confirm) over the 6+1 (STR..SPD + personality?) attribute slots, capping each at 18 and gated on bonus_pool > 0.

evidence.details: Main loop body: reads key via FUN_0000_0098 (key-or-mouse), maps mouse-button to key 1..5 if *0x4fc4==1. key==1: if attr[local_6] > 0 decrement, refund 1 to pool. key==2: prev attr (with wrap to 6). key==3: if attr[local_6] < 18 and pool > 0 increment, drain 1. key==4: next attr (with wrap to 0). key==5: exit only if pool==0. local_16[] holds undo state. Each modification calls 0x2b04 to redraw the panel.

findings.claim: 0x3837 is the personality-traits 'reroll while watching' loop: each iteration rolls rng into *0x55a3 (with optional +1 from some marker byte), redraws screen, breaks on mouse or RETURN. 0x4222 rolls the static personality value (rng(9)+10 = 10..18) into *0x5618 and dispatches to race-specific handler.

evidence.details: 0x3837: clears window 0x56ca, writes title (msg 0x457), `iVar4=1; do { call rng → *0x55a3; if mouse → exit; if kbd → if RETURN exit; } while(iVar4)`; on exit calls 0x2b04 to redraw stats. 0x4222: rolls rng(9)+10 into *0x5618 (range 10..18, 9 values uniform), then if race < 14 calls `(race_handler_table)[race]` to do race-specific post-adjustment (race table at cs:-0x7557 inside wpcmk file).

findings.claim: 0x4589 is the age + carrying-capacity + HP roller. Age = `rng(1000) + 0x19aa` (mean ~18 years in some unit) split across *0x5478/*0x547a. Then per-race compute encum/weight from STR/VIT, and HP_initial = encumbrance * 15 (or * 10 if race == 5 = Faerie).

evidence.details: Sets *0x5616=1, *0x5617=10 (likely level + level-cap), rolls rng(1000)+0x19aa, stores at *0x5478/*0x547a (32-bit). If race < 14: dispatch to race-handler (table at cs:-0x72e6). For 'default' code path: read *0x559c (STR) and *0x559f (VIT), compute `local_6 = (VIT*2 + STR) * 3` and `local_8 = (STR*2 + VIT) * 3`. Adjustments: STR<8 → -1; STR>=16 → +1, local_6+=STR; STR>=18 → +1 again. Similar mods for VIT into local_8. Store at *0x5488/*0x548a (encum_min), *0x548c/*0x548e (encum_max?), HP at *0x5492 = `local_8 * 15`. If race==5 (Faerie): HP = `local_8 * 30 / 3` = local_8 * 10.

findings.claim: 0x4a9a loads one portrait (sprite descriptor) from disk based on video mode and portrait id. 4 templates at 0x53d2..0x53f3 keyed on *0x4fc6 video-mode bitmap; 14 portraits per file × 3 files = 42 total (portrait id cycles 0..41 in 0x4bad mod 0x2a).

evidence.details: 0x4a9a: tests *0x4fc6 against bits 1/2/4/8, picks template 0x53d2/0x53dd/0x53e8/0x53f3 (4 short filename templates — likely 'EFACE??', 'VFACE??', 'CFACE??', 'HFACE??' format). Substitutes record idx via `param_1 / 0xe + '1'` so portrait_id 0..13 → file 1, 14..27 → file 2, 28..41 → file 3. Opens via crt_open (0xf924), seeks via crt_lseek (0xfdbd), reads via crt_read (0xfd6f), closes via crt_dos_close (0xfda5). 0x4bad cycles portrait via *0x560c modulo 42 in a mouse/key loop until user confirms.

findings.claim: 0x28d4 is the train-a-skill flow (skill_pillar=0/1/2/3 → MAGIC/FAITH/PHYSICAL/MENTAL). Iterates 82 skills in the wroot DGROUP table at runtime 0xde..0x322 (6-byte stride), filters by pillar bitmask, lets player pick via 0x229c selection grid, increments skill level at *(0x5498 + skill*4) up to per-attribute cap *(0x549a + skill*4).

evidence.details: 0x28d4: param_3 maps to (local_c, local_e): 0→(8,0x1c), 1→(4,0x1a), 2→(1,0x19), 3→(2,0x1b). local_c is the 'pillar mask', local_e is the 'screen label msg id base'. Iterates 0..0x52 (82 entries) reading byte at `(idx*6 + 0xe3)` (governing-attribute or pillar mask byte), checks `local_c & that_byte != 0` AND `(idx*6 + 0xdf) <= 1` (some level gate), and if both: marks skill available in bitmap 0x55f8 via setbit. 0x229c is the 6-cell grid widget for skill selection. After selection: increments *(0x549a + skill*4) by 1 (clamped to byte at idx*6+0xe0 = max), and *(0x5498 + skill*4) (current level).

findings.claim: 0x001b is the per-record disk I/O (read mode=0 / write mode=1). 0x50f2 picks first empty slot via 0x4ff4. 0x56a0 is the full roster picker. 0x5011 validates name uniqueness via byte-comparator 0x5c42.

evidence.details: 0x001b: opens file via template at *0x4fee (likely 'CHARROST.???'), seeks to `slot * *0x4fd0` (record size from boot config), reads or writes one record buffer (typically 0x1b0 bytes), closes. 0x4ff4: linear scan 0..*0x4fd2 of *(0x4fd8+i) for first 0 (empty slot), returns slot idx or -1. 0x5011: iterate all slots; if occupancy byte != 0, load record, byte-compare names via 0x5c42. 0x56a0: iterates all occupied slots, loads each via 0x001b, packs to display arrays (name @ 0x56d0+i*8, alignment @ 0x5750+i*2, race @ 0x5770+i*2, class @ 0x5790+i*2, source-slot @ 0x57b0+i*2), shows 4-row scrolling list, returns picked source-slot or -1.

findings.claim: 0x3aec loads one item into PC inventory (8 bytes/slot at *0x54b0..0x54b8 etc, max 8 slots). 0x3bfb wraps to load up to 5 starter items. 0x3e51 initializes per-school spell bookmarks at *0x55c2..*0x55cf (14 schools).

evidence.details: 0x3aec calls 0xc31e (the wroot generic data-loader thunk; in wmele it loaded monster types from table-id 1) with table=1 and a 20-byte target buffer. Stores 8-byte item record at `0x54b0 + slot*8`: word at +0 = item id (param_1), word at +2 = some byte, byte at +4/+5, byte at +6 = display-icon-style. Maps source flag-bits (8,4,0x10,0x20,0x2) to target bits (4,8,0x10,0x20,0x40). Increments *0x561c (inventory count). Recomputes *0x5490 (total weight) = sum over inventory of (count * weight). 0x3bfb: do 5x calls if param_i > 0. 0x3e51: 14-iteration loop (0..13 spell schools) with `*(0x55c2+i)=0` clear + call to 3e17 with `param_1[i]*4 - 0x104` (a per-school msg-id base).

findings.claim: 0x3e8c dispatches to class-specific + race-specific finalize handlers (jump-tables at cs:-0x7b9c for class, cs:-0x7a4b for race). Computes derived stats: AC at *0x5563 from DEX/personality; HP at *0x556e modified by VIT; magic-power from INT.

evidence.details: Dispatches: if class < 14 → class-handler-table[class] (cs:-0x7b9c); else if race < 11 → race-handler-table[race] (cs:-0x7a4b); else inline 'human-default' block. Inline block: stat caps DEX>=16 → boost FUN_3e17(6,5) (skill 6 levels up to 5) + FUN_3e17(11,5); INT>=16 → boost FUN_3e17(9,5); SPD>=16 → FUN_3e17(7,5) + FUN_3e17(4,5). Initializes 32-byte combat-stats array at *0x5560..*0x557f (HP, MP, AC, attack mods). DEX adjustments to *0x5563 (AC byte). VIT adjustments to *0x556e (HP byte). Race==5 (Faerie) adjustment to two unnamed bytes (HP penalty + something).

findings.claim: Reusable UI widgets: 0x29c=menu-picker, 0x0f0=text-input editor with backspace/echo/CR-terminate, 0x098=key-or-mouse poll, 0xa99/0xabe/0xaf4=print-msg-at, 0xb1b/0xb44=putchar-at (style 2/4), 0x6af=draw-creation-screen-borders, 0x1cb2=draw-train-screen-borders, 0x689=put-styled-char-at, 0x638=write-msg-centered.

evidence.details: 0x29c is a vertical-menu picker (matches wbase's FUN_025c and wmaze's FUN_1574 pattern: passes msg_id_base, option_flags[], stride/spacing, returns selected index or -1). 0x0f0 is a text-input loop: clears at param_2, accumulates chars on keypress, handles BS=0x08, CR=0x0d, validates 0x20<=c<0x80 (or 0x30<=c<0x3a for numeric mode 1). 0x098 is the poll loop used by all selection screens. 0x689 takes (window, x, y, style_id) and writes the style byte into the window's char-attribute grid at offset 0x10 + (x + y*40)*2 (40-wide grid). 0x6af paints the entire creation panel by 64 calls to 0x689. 0x1cb2 does the same for the 19-wide train panel.

findings.claim: wpcmk shares data tables with wroot at DGROUP runtime offsets: skill table at 0x00de..0x0322 (82 skills × 6 bytes), portrait filename templates at 0x53d2..0x53f3 (4 templates × 11 bytes), msg-id labels 0xcc..0xd3 = 8 attr names, 0xcc=carry-cap label, 0x450..0x452 = race/alignment/class window titles, 0x45c..0x45e = menu headers, 0x453='BONUS POINTS', 0x457='PERSONALITY', 0x458='PORTRAIT', 0x468='Name:', 0x44c='Name:'(alt). The 12 main option msgs are at 0xcc..0xd5, the per-class strings encoding requirements at file offset (per the wbase delta law) somewhere ≥0x4dc6.

evidence.details: Inferred from the load_msg_into_buf (0xc1f7) calls and the c2db msg-id arguments across all UI functions. The skill table at runtime 0xde is referenced directly via cs:-style addressing in 0x28d4 (which iterates 82 entries × 6 bytes = 492 bytes). The portrait templates at 0x53d2..0x53f3 are 4 × 0x11 = 0x44 bytes (each is a near-string with placeholder for digit), referenced by 0x4a9a's video-mode-based template selection.
